review.notes: Drafted for #11. The polygon is the sector as established on D-Day (where the assault actually landed), not as planned. Geometry derivation: Map VII of Utah Beach to Cherbourg (Commons scan, 1844x1142 px) has a 500-yard scale bar (163 px, so about 2.8 m per pixel) and a north arrow. On it, Uncle Red and Tare Green as established on D-Day meet at the Exit 2 road, Uncle Red running about 266 px (about 750 m) south of it and Tare Green about 263 px (about 740 m) north. As planned, Uncle Red ran from 424 px to 752 px and Tare Green from 752 px to 1122 px north of Exit 2. Exit 2 (Causeway 2, towards Sainte-Marie-du-Mont) was matched to the present-day D913, which meets the coast road at -1.17687, 49.4151; that point was projected onto the present-day OSM coastline and the map distances were laid off along the coastline from there. Seaward depth is the distance from the high-water mark to the low-water mark measured on Map VII at each sector boundary (about 0.8 to 1.4 km), applied perpendicular to the general line of the coast (bearing 319 degrees). Cross-check: Map VII's Exit 3 road, transformed the same way, falls within about 80 m of the point where the present-day D67 meets the coast. Accuracy is "approximate" because the 1944 map was georeferenced by hand from one road junction, a scale bar and the modern coastline, and the 1944 high- and low-water lines are not today's. Company and wave allocations for tanks and engineers come from Map VII, which shows the landing plan as of 24 May 1944; Wikipedia confirms the rifle companies landed as planned on each beach, but no readable source says whether the tank and engineer detachments landed on the beach the plan gave them. Books Wikipedia cites (Ford & Zaloga 2009; Balkoski 2005) could not be read; see utah-beach.json for the hosts that were refused.

summary.text: The left-hand (southern) of the two assault beaches at Utah. As planned, Uncle Red lay immediately south of Tare Green, opposite Exit 3; after currents set the craft south it was established south of Exit 2 instead. Companies E and F of the 8th Infantry landed here in the first wave at 06:30, with Company F under Leonard T. Schroeder reported as the first to reach the beach, and Companies G and H followed in the second wave. Companies E and F took strongpoint WN4 at La Dune after a short fight and then moved south towards Causeway 1; Companies G and H went south along the beach, through a minefield and machine-gun fire, and captured strongpoint WN3 at Beau Guillot.
